chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hafs ibn Awn, who raised it (mursal), said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A moment from a just Imam is superior to seventy years of worship, and a hadd penalty enacted for the sake of God on earth is superior to forty mornings of rain.'

key_terms.إمام عدل: A just Imam — in Shia tradition, this refers specifically to the divinely-appointed Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt; in broader usage it can mean any just ruler
key_terms.حد: Hadd (plural: hudud) — divinely-prescribed legal penalties for specific offenses mentioned in the Quran, such as theft, adultery, and slander
key_terms.ساعة: A moment or hour — here used to mean a brief period of time, emphasizing that even a short duration of just rule has immense value
key_terms.يُقام لله: Enacted for the sake of God — meaning the penalty is carried out with sincerity and in accordance with divine law, not out of personal vengeance

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about just leadership and implementing Islamic penalties?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) declares that a brief period of just governance by a legitimate Imam surpasses decades of individual worship in merit, and that implementing divinely-mandated criminal penalties (hudud) is more beneficial than rain — which was the most vital natural blessing in arid Arabia. This hadith comes from the opening chapter on identifying Islamic legal penalties (hudud), emphasizing that applying divine law is an act of supreme worship that benefits the whole community by maintaining social order, deterrence, and moral purity. The comparison to seventy years of worship and forty mornings of rain uses hyperbolic language conventional in hadith literature to underscore the supreme importance of just governance and divine law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Hafs Bin Awn, raising it, said,

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘A moment from a just Imamasws is superior to worship of seventy years, and a Penalty (Hadd) established for the Sake of Allahazwj in the earth is superior that the rain of forty mornings’.
